bug_description.original: Container-overflow READ 8 in jxl::InvSqueeze, called via jxl::Transform::Inverse and jxl::Image::undo_transforms. Crash State: jxl::InvSqueeze / jxl::Transform::Inverse / jxl::Image::undo_transforms. Sanitizer: address (ASAN). Recommended Security Severity: Medium.
bug_description.normalized: In libjxl's modular decoding path, MetaSqueeze increments Image::nb_meta_channels when squeeze parameters target meta channels, but InvSqueeze does not decrement it when reversing the transform. This desynchronization causes the meta/non-meta channel boundary tracked by nb_meta_channels to drift from the actual channel layout across stacked transforms. When undo_transforms reverses the transform chain, the stale nb_meta_channels leaves the channel vector in a state inconsistent with the squeeze parameters stored during the forward pass, causing InvSqueeze to compute a residual channel index rc that exceeds the vector's logical size, resulting in a container-overflow out-of-bounds read of 8 bytes.

source.description: MetaSqueeze increments nb_meta_channels when squeeze parameters target meta channels, creating the state asymmetry that InvSqueeze fails to reverse.
source.value_from: JXL bitstream: squeeze parameters begin_c, num_c deserialized from attacker-controlled input
source.note: When beginc < nb_meta_channels, MetaSqueeze increments nb_meta_channels by num_c to account for newly inserted residual channels being categorized as meta channels. This increment was added in PR #331 but the corresponding decrement in InvSqueeze was omitted.

root_cause.description: InvSqueeze omits the nb_meta_channels decrement that must mirror MetaSqueeze's increment, causing channel layout desynchronization across stacked transforms during reverse application.
root_cause.note: The fix adds: if (beginc < input.nb_meta_channels) { input.nb_meta_channels -= parameters[i].num_c; } before the inner channel loop, restoring the symmetric invariant.

sink.description: Out-of-bounds read of input.channel[rc] where rc exceeds the vector's logical size due to the desynchronized channel layout.
sink.note: ASAN reports container-overflow READ of 8 bytes at offset 704 in a 896-byte allocation; rc indexes past the vector's logical end (672 bytes) into allocated-but-erased storage (0xfc shadow).

parser_admitted.description: Bitstream header and transform list decoded via Bundle::Read; squeeze transform params extracted from the crafted JXL input. MetaApply is called for each transform in forward order (line 393-394), building up the channel layout. undo_transforms later reverses them (modular_image.cc:17-28), popping transforms from the back and calling Transform::Inverse for each.

tainted_value_origin.description: Squeeze transform parameters (begin_c, num_c, in_place, horizontal) are deserialized from the attacker-controlled JXL bitstream and stored as the image's transform list.

coarse_trace.summary: Deserialize squeeze transforms from the JXL bitstream and call MetaApply for each, which invokes MetaSqueeze to update the channel layout and nb_meta_channels.
For meta-channel squeezes (beginc < nb_meta_channels), increment nb_meta_channels by num_c and insert residual channels into the channel vector.

During undo_transforms, InvSqueeze processes squeeze parameters in reverse, computing residual channel index rc and erasing residuals. nb_meta_channels is NOT decremented, desynchronizing the channel boundary from the actual layout across stacked transforms.
Container-overflow: input.channel[rc] reads past the vector's logical end due to desynchronized channel layout. ASAN detects the 8-byte OOB read.

fine_trace.note: Squeeze transform parameters deserialized from the crafted JXL bitstream are assigned to the image's transform list. Each squeeze transform carries begin_c, num_c, in_place, and horizontal fields that control which channels are squeezed and where residuals are placed. MetaApply is then called for each transform in forward order (line 393-394).

For squeeze parameters where beginc < nb_meta_channels, MetaSqueeze increments nb_meta_channels by num_c to track that the inserted residual channels are themselves meta channels. The channel vector grows as residual channels are inserted at the computed offset (line 272). This increment was added in PR #331; the corresponding decrement in InvSqueeze was not added.

InvSqueeze iterates squeeze parameters in reverse to undo MetaSqueeze. It does NOT decrement nb_meta_channels when beginc < nb_meta_channels. After each iteration erases residual channels from the vector (line 310-311), the channel vector shrinks but nb_meta_channels retains the inflated value from MetaSqueeze. When multiple transforms are stacked, this desync causes the channel layout at the time of a subsequent InvSqueeze call to differ from the layout the stored squeeze parameters assumed.

The residual channel index rc is derived from offset (endc + 1 for in_place, or channel.size() + beginc - endc - 1 otherwise). Due to the desynchronized nb_meta_channels across stacked transforms, the channel vector's logical size no longer accommodates the residual positions expected by the stored squeeze parameters. CheckMetaSqueezeParams (line 287) only validates beginc and endc against channel.size(), not the derived residual index rc.

Container-overflow: rc indexes past the channel vector's logical end into previously allocated but erased storage. ASAN detects an 8-byte read (the .w field of a Channel object) at address 0x618000000740, 704 bytes into a 896-byte heap region, 32 bytes past the container's logical boundary at 672 bytes.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Allocation is in MetaSqueeze (channel.insert at line 272) which grows the vector; the root cause is InvSqueeze's failure to decrement nb_meta_channels, causing the layout to desynchronize after subsequent erases shrink the vector below the expected residual positions.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Attacker-controlled squeeze parameters (begin_c, num_c) from the JXL bitstream determine MetaSqueeze's nb_meta_channels increment and InvSqueeze's offset/rc computation, creating the OOB access path.

format.name: JPEG XL
format.contract: A crafted JPEG XL bitstream whose modular transform list contains squeeze parameters that target meta channels (begin_c < nb_meta_channels), causing MetaSqueeze to increment nb_meta_channels. When InvSqueeze later reverses the transforms without decrementing nb_meta_channels, the channel layout desynchronizes across the stacked transform chain, leading to a container-overflow out-of-bounds read.
